text: Yeah. So I'm Harry Halpin, I'm the CEO and co founder of NIM Technologies and we are what's called a network level privacy project. So Brendan has a browser and that browser defends your application level privacy when you're browsing the Internet. And you can run this browser on trusted hardware or do computations on hardware of your choice. But the fact of the matter is every time you send a TCPIP or UDP packet, anytime you send a packet over the Internet, the IP address on that packet is revealed. So you can use software like Tor or VPN to help stop adversaries like Chainalysis or the NSA or cyber criminals from discovering your IP address and then locating out who you are when you're doing, for example, a Bitcoin or whatever transaction. However, a very powerful adversary can just watch the network's data flowing in and out and they can figure out the timing, the volume and the patterns of Internet traffic that you are sending. What a mix that does is we basically take those individual packets, we encrypt them and we shuffle them. That's mixing and then we send them out. And that really provides resistance against even what we call global passive adversaries that can watch the entire network. So we're one level below chain. So even if you use technology such as zcash shielded transactions or Monero ring signatures to hide some on chain data, the network level is still going to leak your identity and the kind of transaction data. So we really do recommend people look into using our technology and mixed networks in general to basically defend their privacy on the network level. And if you use our technology in combination with say Brave, you get something which we call full stack Privacy or holistic privacy where you can really defend all levels of your data from outside surveillance. We're a very proud graduate of the first finance incubator back in 2018.
